references.text: The Nile (היאר) is mentioned as an important place in Egypt, where Moses himself was found as an infant.
The staff that was turned into a snake (נחש) - the same staff Moses is now to take with him to Pharaoh.
The staff that turns into a snake (נחש) is used as a sign before Pharaoh, the same staff mentioned here.
Moses is told to stand before Pharaoh in the morning (בבקר) by the water, a similar instruction as here.
God commands Moses to stand before Pharaoh early in the morning (בבקר), the same pattern as in this verse.
The first plague at the Nile follows immediately after this instruction, where the staff is used to strike the water.
Pharaoh is compared to a great sea creature (תנים) in the Nile, showing Pharaoh's connection to the river.
Complementary parts of the same confrontation: instructions to meet Pharaoh with the staff (7:15) and the actual transformation into a snake (7:9).
Theological contrast: God's demand for full liberation (7:15) meets Pharaoh's attempt at compromise (8:24).
Parallel use of the staff over water: confrontation (snake) by the river versus deliverance (parting) at the sea.
Connection between the preparation of the miracle (grasping the snake/staff in 4:4) and its use before Pharaoh (7:15).
